    // The constant strain inside one tetrahedral cell, as the symmetric tensor of
    // TENSOR strains — off-diagonal entries are half the engineering shears,
    // which is what `StrainState3D` documents.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinitesimal_strain_theory)
    ElementStrain(c: TetrahedronCell, positions: Array<Point3D>,
        displacements: Array<Vector3D>): StrainState3D
    {
        var gradients = c.ShapeGradients(positions);
        var nodes = c.CellVertices;
        var nodal = 4.MapRange(i => displacements[nodes[i].Value]);
        return StrainState3D(SymmetricMatrix3x3(
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 0),
            (DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 1)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 0)) * 0.5,
            (DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 2)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 2, 0)) * 0.5,
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 1),
            (DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 2)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 2, 1)) * 0.5,
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 2, 2)));
    }
```

    // The constant in-plane strain inside one plane triangle. ShearXY is the
    // ENGINEERING shear strain (twice the tensor component), which is what
    // `StrainState2D` documents.
    ElementStrain(f: TriangleFace, positions: Array<Point2D>,
        displacements: Array<Vector2D>): StrainState2D
    {
        var gradients = f.ShapeGradients(positions);
        var nodes = f.Vertices;
        var nodal = 3.MapRange(i => Vector3D(displacements[nodes[i].Value].X,
            displacements[nodes[i].Value].Y, 0.0));
        return StrainState2D(
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 0),
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 1),
            DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 0, 1)
                + DisplacementGradient(nodal, gradients, 1, 0));
    }
```
